findings.issue_text: [BUG] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached model is concurrently invalidated, and callers that unbox the Long (e.g. arithmetic or primitive assignment in sub-group pagination/count code) will throw NullPointerException on that return value, converting the original NPE into the same failure at a different call site. A concurrent invalidation between isUpdated() and the model fetch produces a null Long that crashes the caller with NPE instead of falling back to a store re-read; the correct fix is to invalidate the cached entry and fetch from the session/store, not to return null.

[BUG] The fix guards only getSubGroupsCount(); sibling GroupAdapter methods on the same concurrent-invalidation path (e.g. getSubGroupsStream just above at line 271, and other delegating methods in this class) still call getGroupModel() directly and will still NPE when the cached model is nulled concurrently. The PR's stated goal 'fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException' is only partially achieved: any read of sub-groups (stream) or other delegated state racing an invalidation throws the same NPE the test claims to guard against, so the acceptance criterion is not met.

[BUG] The reader thread is never joined and caughtExceptions is asserted immediately after deletedAll.set(true), so an in-flight request that throws after the flag is set is recorded after the assertion executes and the failure is never observed. The test can pass (Matchers.empty() succeeds) even when the NPE it is meant to catch occurs in the final in-flight iteration, giving false verification of the fix; the thread must be joined (or exceptions re-checked after join) before asserting.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is a non-daemon Thread with an unbounded while loop; if any statement between thread start and deletedAll.set(true) throws (e.g. a delete fails), the thread spins forever and leaks, hanging the test JVM's shutdown for non-daemon threads. A failing assertion or exception in the delete loop leaves the busy-loop thread running for the remainder of the suite, wasting CPU and potentially timing out the test runner; wrap the loop body/flag in try/finally or use a daemon thread with a join timeout.

[ADVISORY] The new test only exercises top-level group listing; it never invokes getSubGroupsCount() (the method actually changed in GroupAdapter), so the modified code path has no coverage in this diff. A regression in getSubGroupsCount()'s new null-return logic would pass this test suite; adding sub-group count reads (e.g. fetching a group with children) to the concurrent loop would close the gap.

[ADVISORY] Deleting groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement removes the only place the diff documents how search filtering treats groups with sub-groups; any caller outside GroupUtils that relied on this behavior (group path elements retained during search) silently loses it unless migrated elsewhere in the same release. Out-of-tree or same-release callers referencing this utility (it is in a public utils package) fail to compile, or behavior for hierarchical search changes without a replacement verified in this diff.

[BUG] The fix replaces one NPE with another: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the cached model has been evicted, and every caller that unboxes the Long (e.g. `long count = getSubGroupsCount()`, arithmetic, or REST serialization paths expecting a value) throws NullPointerException exactly as before. Under concurrent invalidation the same NPE the PR claims to fix still occurs, only moved from the model dereference to the caller's unboxing of the null Long; the change also silently widens the interface contract from Long to nullable Long without any caller-side null handling being added in this diff.

[BUG] The reader thread is never joined and the assertion `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs immediately after the deletion loop, so exceptions thrown between the loop's last iteration and `deletedAll.set(true)` (or in-flight during the assertion) are missed, and the bare non-daemon thread keeps spinning forever if the test fails. The test is flaky in the false-negative direction — it can pass despite the concurrency bug it was written to catch — and on a failed run the leaked spinning thread makes the JVM suite hang.

[ADVISORY] Deletion of the private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement is unrelated cleanup bundled into an NPE-fix PR and is not traceable to the stated intent. Reviewers and future bisection on this PR must reason about a services-layer search-helper removal that has no connection to the Infinispan cache concurrency fix; if the helper turns out to be referenced elsewhere the build breaks at merge rather than in review.

[ADVISORY] The eviction race is patched only in getSubGroupsCount while sibling methods in the same class (e.g. getSubGroupsStream and other modelSupplier-consuming accessors) follow the identical dereference pattern and are left untouched. The next concurrent-access report lands on an adjacent method with the same root cause, and the null-tolerant pattern established here has to be re-derived per-method instead of centralized in modelSupplier handling.

[ADVISORY] The new test exercises only the admin REST listing path; it never asserts the fixed code path's contract (that a count/read during concurrent delete returns a defined value rather than null), so a regression that changes the null return to a different wrong value still passes. The null return introduced in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount (the actual under-scoped defect) is invisible to this test because the REST layer may tolerate or mask the null, leaving the P1 unfixed-but-green.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the cached model has been evicted instead of a real count, changing the method's sentinel semantics from 'NPE risk during eviction' to 'null meaning not available'. Any caller that unboxes the Long (e.g. assigns to long, arithmetic, or comparison in pagination code paths) now gets a NullPointerException at the call site instead of the previous behavior; null propagates 'cache entry gone' as a value where the contract expects a count, so concurrent eviction converts one crash site into many scattered unboxing crashes.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is not joined and uses an unsynchronized visibility handoff: deletedAll is a plain AtomicBoolean set after the delete loop, but exceptions appended after the assertion window are lost. Exceptions caught by the reader thread in the interval after deletedAll.set(true) but before the thread exits are added to caughtExceptions after assertThat runs, so a real concurrent NPE can slip through and the test passes green while production fails — a flaky stand-in guard.

[ADVISORY] Removal of groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement eliminates the 'group name contains search OR has subgroups' behavior; if any remaining caller still relied on path-element matching semantics, sub-group containment during search is now lost. If this helper was the only place implementing parent-group matching for search, hierarchical search results change for callers that depended on a parent matching when a child matched; deletion is only correct if all callers were also removed, which the diff does not show.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the underlying cached model has been invalidated, silently changing the method's contract from always returning a count to returning a nullable Long Callers that unbox the result into a primitive long (e.g. arithmetic or long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) will throw NullPointerException on concurrent invalidation, converting the original NPE from a race window into a deterministic failure path introduced by the fix itself

[BUG] The PR titled 'Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException' deletes groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement without any caller removal in the diff, silently changing the objective to include removing search-matching behavior If any retained call site still references the method the code fails to compile; if callers were pre-removed, the behavior change (search semantics) was never part of the stated NPE-fix intent and shipped without explicit acceptance

[ADVISORY] The concurrency test's reader thread is not joined and its exceptions are only observed until deletedAll is set, so exceptions thrown after the last delete completes are silently ignored A race-induced NPE that fires after the deletes finish is never reported, giving the test false confidence that it actually verifies the fix under the intended concurrent-access conditions

[ADVISORY] Returning null from getSubGroupsCount diverges from the parallel behavior of other GroupAdapter methods in the same class, which return stream/count values directly, creating inconsistent invalidation handling that the next similar bug fix will likely copy incorrectly Future maintainers fixing sibling count/stream methods in this cache layer will have two conflicting patterns to choose from, and picking the null-return one propagates the contract change to other call sites

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is never joined and the assertion can run while a read request is still in flight, so a NullPointerException triggered during the deletes can be recorded after assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) has already passed. On a fast/loaded CI machine the test intermittently passes despite the exact NPE it was written to catch — a false-confidence concurrency test that hides regressions in the cache fix.

[ADVISORY] The test's race coverage is timing-dependent: if the reader thread is slow to schedule, all 100 deletes can complete (deletedAll set true) before the thread performs even one groups() listing, so the loop exits immediately and the test passes without ever exercising the concurrent read/delete path it is named for. The test can pass vacuously on any CI run where thread startup loses the race, giving green coverage of the KEYCLOAK NPE fix without the vulnerable code path ever being executed.

[ADVISORY] The test only asserts that no exception was thrown; it never verifies the fixed behavior itself (that getSubGroupsCount/subgroup reads return correct data or a well-defined result when the cached model is null), so any change that returns a wrong-but-non-throwing count passes. A regression where the cache returns a wrong subgroup count or empty representation under concurrent delete would not be detected — the test validates absence of 500s only, not correctness of the new null-handling branch in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached model has been invalidated, but the Long return type means every caller that unboxes it (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount(), or JAX-RS count endpoints serializing a primitive) throws a NullPointerException — the diff swaps the original NPE inside the cache for a new NPE at the call site, surfacing as a 500 instead of a valid count response. When a group entry is invalidated/evited concurrently (the very race this PR fixes for other methods), an admin REST call that reads the sub-group count crashes with a raw NullPointerException and a 500, while the API contract promises a numeric count; callers doing long unboxing fail identically.

[ADVISORY] groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement is deleted with no replacement in this diff, but its callers (sub-group search/filter paths it previously guarded) are not shown being updated, so any remaining call site in the same tree now fails to compile or the filtering behavior it provided is silently dropped. If a caller remains, the build breaks; if the caller was removed elsewhere, sub-group search previously returned ancestor groups whose children matched the search (the findAny().isPresent() clause) and that behavior is now silently gone for users filtering sub-groups.

adjudication.rationale: The added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` only spawns a reader thread calling `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` during deletions and then asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. It does not assert any correctness of subgroup counts or returned data, so the new null-handling branch in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`) could return an incorrect-but-non-throwing value and the test would still pass. This is a specific coverage gap tied to the newly introduced behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached model has been invalidated, but the Long return type means every caller that unboxes it (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount(), or JAX-RS count endpoints serializing a primitive) throws a NullPointerException — the diff swaps the original NPE inside the cache for a new NPE at the call site, surfacing as a 500 instead of a valid count response. When a group entry is invalidated/evited concurrently (the very race this PR fixes for other methods), an admin REST call that reads the sub-group count crashes with a raw NullPointerException and a 500, while the API contract promises a numeric count; callers doing long unboxing fail identically.
